A dog food company records data on the number of dogs $(x)$ sheltered at some kennels across the country and the corresponding amount of dog food $y$ (in kilograms) consumed in a month. The scatter plot for the data and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above. 

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted data point?

current_example.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/089aa0d861b267352f9e5d83f47a00d5fd330f0f280268783e5a8e88cf947a98.png)

The scatter plot for the data sets $x$ and $y$ of paired observations and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above. According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted datapoint?
current_example.worked_solution:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

$$
\textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated}
$$

 

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(82,70).$ So, our actual value is $y=70.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=82$ has the $y$-coordinate $65.$ So, our estimated value is $\widehat{y}=65.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/99e3741f602802e636e2e49ef755954343079b8c0d98453dac9364ddc08ef16f.png)

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Residual} & =\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated} \\  & =y-\overset{^}{y} \\  & =70-65 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residual is $5.$
